١٥١١٨ — عن عباد بن الوليد بن عبادة بن الصامت قال: خرجت أنا وأبي نطلب العلم في هذا الحي من الأنصار قبل أن يهلكوا، فكان أول من لقينا أبا اليسر صاحب رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، ومعه غلام له، معه ضمامة من صحف، وعلى أبي اليسر بردة ومعافري، وعلى غلامه بردة ومعافري، فقال له أبي: يا عم، إني أرى في وجهك سفعة من غضب. قال: أجل، كان لي على فلان بن فلان الحرامي مال، فأتيت أهله فسلمت، فقلت: ثم هو؟ قالوا: لا. فخرج علي ابن له جفر، فقلت له: أين أبوك؟ قال: سمع صوتك فدخل أريكة أمي. فقلت: اخرج إلي، فقد علمت أين أنت. فخرج، فقلت: ما حملك على أن اختبأت مني؟ قال: أنا واللّٰه أحدثك ثم لا أكذبك، خشيت واللّٰه أن أحدثك فأكذبك، وأن أعدك فأخلفك، وكنت صاحب رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، وكنت واللّٰه معسرًا. قال قلت: آللّٰه؟ قال: اللّٰه. قلت: آللّٰه؟ قال: اللّٰه. قلت: آللّٰه؟ قال: اللّٰه. قال: فأتى بصحيفته فمحاها بيده، فقال: إن وجدت قضاء فاقضني، وإلا أنت في حل، فأشهد بصر عيني هاتين - ووضع إصبعيه على عينيه - وسمع أذني هاتين، ووعاه قلبي هذا - وأشار إلى مناط قلبه - رسول اللّٰه ﷺ وهو يقول:
((من أنظر معسرًا، أو وضع عنه، أظله اللّٰه في ظله)).
قال: فقلت له أنا: يا عم، لو أنك أخذت بردة غلامك وأعطيته معافريك، وأخذت معافريه وأعطيته بردتك، فكانت عليك حلة وعليه حلة. فمسح رأسي وقال: اللهم بارك فيه. يا ابن أخي، بصر عيني هاتين، وسمع أذني هاتين، ووعاه قلبي هذا - وأشار إلى مناط قلبه - رسول اللّٰه ﷺ وهو يقول:
((أطعموهم مما تأكلون، وألبسوهم مما تلبسون)).
وكان أن أعطيه من متاع الدنيا أهون علي من أن يأخذ من حسناتي يوم القيامة.
ثم مضينا حتى أتينا جابر بن عبد اللّٰه في مسجده، وهو يصلي في ثوب واحد مشتملًا به، فتخطيت القوم حتى جلست بينه وبين القبلة، فقلت: يرحمك اللّٰه، أتصلي في ثوب واحد ورداؤك إلى جنبك؟ قال: فقال بيده في صدري هكذا، وفرق بين أصابعه وقوسها: أردت أن يدخل علي الأحمق مثلك، فيراني كيف أصنع، فيصنع مثله.
أتانا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ في مسجدنا هذا، وفي يده عرجون ابن طاب، فرأى في قبلة المسجد نخامة فحكها بالعرجون، ثم أقبل علينا فقال:
((أيكم يحب أن يعرض اللّٰه عنه؟)).
قال: فخشعنا، ثم قال:
((أيكم يحب أن يعرض اللّٰه عنه؟)).
قال: فخشعنا، ثم قال:
((أيكم يحب أن يعرض اللّٰه عنه؟)).
قلنا: لا أينا يا رسول اللّٰه! قال:
((فإن أحدكم إذا قام يصلي، فإن اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى قبل وجهه، فلا يبصقن قبل وجهه، ولا عن يمينه، وليبصق عن يساره تحت رجله اليسرى، فإن عجلت به بادرة، فليقل بثوبه هكذا)).
ثم طوى ثوبه بعضه على بعض، فقال:
((أروني عبيرًا)).
فقام فتى من الحي يشتد إلى أهله، فجاء بخلوق في راحته، فأخذه رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فجعله على رأس العرجون، ثم لطخ به على أثر النخامة.
فقال جابر: فمن هناك جعلتم الخلوق في مساجدكم.
سرنا مع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ في غزوة بطن بواط، وهو يطلب المجدي بن عمرو الجهني، وكان الناضح يعقبه منا الخمسة والستة والسبعة، فدارت عقبة رجل من الأنصار على ناضح له، فأناخه فركبه، ثم بعثه فتلدن عليه بعض التلدن، فقال له: شأ، لعنك اللّٰه. فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((من هذا اللاعن بعيره؟)).
قال: أنا يا رسول اللّٰه. قال:
((انزل عنه، فلا تصحبنا بملعون، لا تدعوا على أنفسكم، ولا تدعوا على أولادكم، ولا تدعوا على أموالكم، لا توافقوا من اللّٰه ساعة يسأل فيها عطاء، فيستجيب لكم)).
سرنا مع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ حتى إذا كانت عشيشية ودنونا ماء من مياه العرب، قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((من رجل يتقدمنا فيمدر الحوض فيشرب ويسقينا؟)).
قال جابر: فقمت، فقلت: هذا رجل يا رسول اللّٰه. فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((أي رجل مع جابر؟)).
فقام جبار بن صخر، فانطلقنا إلى البئر، فنزعنا في الحوض سجلًا أو سجلين، ثم مدرناه، ثم نزعنا فيه حتى أَفْهَقْناه، فكان أول طالع علينا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فقال:
((أتأذنان؟)).
قلنا: نعم يا رسول اللّٰه. فأشرع ناقته فشربت، شنق لها فشجت فبالت، ثم عدل بها فأناخها، ثم جاء رسول اللّٰه ﷺ إلى الحوض فتوضأ منه، ثم قمت فتوضأت من متوضأ رسول اللّٰه ﷺ.
فذهب جبار بن صخر يقضي حاجته، فقام رسول اللّٰه ﷺ ليصلي، وكانت علي بردة، ذهبت أن أخالف بين طرفيها فلم تبلغ لي، وكانت لها ذباذب، فنكستها، ثم خالفت بين طرفيها، ثم تواقصت عليها، ثم جئت حتى قمت عن يسار رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فأخذ بيدي فأدارني حتى أقامني عن يمينه، ثم جاء جبار بن صخر فتوضأ، ثم جاء فقام عن يسار رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فأخذ رسول اللّٰه ﷺ بيدينا جميعًا، فدفعنا حتى أقامنا خلفه، فجعل رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يرمقني وأنا لا أشعر، ثم فطنت به، فقال هكذا بيده، يعني: شد وسطك. فلما فرغ رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قال:
((يا جابر)).
قلت: لبيك يا رسول اللّٰه. قال:
((إذا كان واسعًا فخالف بين طرفيه، وإذا كان ضيقًا فاشدده على حقوك)).
سرنا مع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، وكان قوت كل رجل منا في كل يوم تمرة، فكان يمصها ثم يصرها في ثوبه، وكنا نختبط بقسينا ونأكل، حتى قرحت أشداقنا، فأقسم أخطئها رجل منا يومًا، فانطلقنا به ننعشه، فشهدنا أنه لم يعطها، فأعطيها فقام فأخذها.
سرنا مع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ حتى نزلنا واديًا أفيح، فذهب رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يقضي حاجته، فاتبعته بإداوة من ماء، فنظر رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فلم ير شيئًا يستتر به، فإذا شجرتان بشاطئ الوادي، فانطلق رسول اللّٰه ﷺ إلى إحداهما فأخذ بغصن من أغصانها، فقال:
((انقادي علي بإذن اللّٰه)).
فانقادت معه كالبعير المخشوش الذي يصانع قائده، حتى أتى الشجرة الأخرى، فأخذ بغصن من أغصانها، فقال:
((انقادي علي بإذن اللّٰه)).
فانقادت معه كذلك، حتى إذا كان بالمنصف مما بينهما، لأم بينهما - يعني جمعهما - فقال:
((التئما علي بإذن اللّٰه)).
فالتأمتا.
قال جابر: فخرجت أحضر مخافة أن يحس رسول اللّٰه ﷺ بقربي فيبتعد، (وقال محمد بن عباد: فيتبعد)، فجلست أحدث نفسي، فحانت مني لفتة، فإذا أنا برسول اللّٰه ﷺ مقبلًا، وإذا الشجرتان قد افترقتا، فقامت كل واحدة منهما على ساق، فرأيت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ وقف وقفة، فقال برأسه هكذا - وأشار أبو إسماعيل برأسه يمينًا وشمالًا - ثم أقبل. فلما انتهى إلي قال:
((يا جابر، هل رأيت مقامي؟)).
قلت: نعم يا رسول اللّٰه. قال:
((فانطلق إلى الشجرتين، فاقطع من كل واحدة منهما غصنًا، فأقبل بهما، حتى إذا قمت مقامي فأرسل غصنًا عن يمينك وغصنًا عن يسارك)).
قال جابر: فقمت فأخذت حجرًا فكسرته وحسرته، فانذلق لي، فأتيت الشجرتين فقطعت من كل واحدة منهما غصنًا، ثم أقبلت أجرهما حتى قمت مقام رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، أرسلت غصنًا عن يميني وغصنًا عن يساري، ثم لحقته فقلت: قد فعلت يا رسول اللّٰه، فعم ذاك؟ قال:
((إني مررت بقبرين يعذبان، فأحببت بشفاعتي أن يرفه عنهما، ما دام الغصنان رطبين)).
قال: فأتينا العسكر، فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((يا جابر، ناد بوضوء)).
فقلت: ألا وضوء؟ ألا وضوء؟ ألا وضوء؟ قال قلت: يا رسول اللّٰه، ما وجدت في الركب من قطرة. وكان رجل من الأنصار يبرد لرسول اللّٰه ﷺ الماء في أشجاب له على حمارة من جريد، قال: فقال لي:
((انطلق إلى فلان ابن فلان الأنصاري، فانظر هل في أشجابه من شيء؟)).
قال: فانطلقت إليه فنظرت فيها فلم أجد فيها إلا قطرة في عزلاء شجب منها، لو أني أفرغه لشربه يابسه، فأتيت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فقلت: يا رسول اللّٰه، إني لم أجد فيها إلا قطرة في عزلاء شجب منها، لو أني أفرغه لشربه يابسه. قال:
((اذهب فأتني به)).
فأتيته به، فأخذه بيده فجعل يتكلم بشيء لا أدري ما هو، ويغمزه بيديه، ثم أعطانيه فقال:
((يا جابر، ناد بجفنة)).
فقلت: يا جفنة الركب! فأُتيت بها تُحمل، فوضعتها بين يديه، فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ بيده في الجفنة هكذا، فبسطها وفرق بين أصابعه، ثم وضعها في قعر الجفنة، وقال:
((خذ يا جابر، فصب علي، وقل: باسم اللّٰه)).
فصببت عليه وقلت: باسم اللّٰه، فرأيت الماء يفور من بين أصابع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، ثم فارت الجفنة ودارت حتى امتلأت، فقال:
((يا جابر، ناد من كان له حاجة بماء)).
قال: فأتى الناس فاستقوا حتى رووا، قال فقلت: هل بقي أحد له حاجة؟ فرفع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يده من الجفنة وهي ملأى.
وشكا الناس إلى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ الجوع، فقال:
((عسى اللّٰه أن يطعمكم)).
فأتينا سيف البحر، فزخر البحر زخرة، فألقى دابة، فأورينا على شقها النار، فاطبخنا واشتوينا وأكلنا حتى شبعنا. قال جابر: فدخلت أنا وفلان وفلان، حتى عد خمسة، في حجاج عينها، ما يرانا أحد، حتى خرجنا، فأخذنا ضلعًا من أضلاعها فقوسناه، ثم دعونا بأعظم رجل في الركب، وأعظم جمل في الركب، وأعظم كفل في الركب، فدخل تحته ما يطأطئ رأسه.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٣٠٠٦-٣٠١٤).
شرح الكلمات الغريبة
قوله: “معه ضمامة من صحف”: أي رزمة يضم بعضها إلى بعض.
قوله: “بردة”: وهي شملة مخططة.
قوله: “معافري”: نوع من الثياب يعمل بقرية تسمى معافر.
قوله: “سفعة من غضب”: علامة وتغير.
قوله: “جفر”: هو الذي قارب البلوغ.
قوله: “مناط قلبه”: هو عرق معلق بالقلب.
قوله: “حلة”: هي إزار ورداء.
قوله: “عرجون”: هو الغصن.
قوله: “ابن طاب”: نوع من التمر.
قوله: “عبيرًا”: قال أبو عبيد: هو الزعفران وحده. وقال الأصمعي: هو أخلاط من الطيب تجمع بالزعفران.
قوله: “بخلوق”: هو طيب من أنواع مختلفة يجمع بالزعفران، وهو العبير كما قال الأصمعي.
قوله: “بطن بواط”: هو جبل من جبال جهينة.
قوله: “الناضح”: أي البعير الذي يستقى عليه.
قوله: “شأ لعنك اللّٰه”: هي كلمة زجر للبعير، يقال: شأشأت البعير إذا زجرته وقلت له: شأ.
قوله: “فيمدر الحوض”: أي يطينه ويصلحه.
قوله: “حتى أفهقناه”: أي ملأناه.
قوله: “فأشرع ناقته”: أرسل رأسها في الماء لتشرب.
قوله: “شنق لها”: يقال: شنقها وأشنقها أي كففها بزمامها وأنت راكبها.
قوله: “فشجت”: يقال: فشج البعير إذا فرج بين رجليه للبول.
قوله: “ذباذب”: واحدها ذبذب، سميت بذلك لأنها تتذبذب على صاحبها إذا مشى - أي أنها تتحرك وتضطرب -.
قوله: “فنكستها”: أي قلبته، ومنه قيل: ولد منكوس، إذا خرج رجلاه قبل رأسه.
قوله: “تواقصت عليها”: أي أمسكت عليها بعنقي وحنيته عليها لئلا تسقط.
قوله: “فاشدده على حقوك”: هو معقد الإزار، المراد هنا: أن يبلغ السرة.
قوله: “وكنا نختبط بقسينا”: معنى نختبط نضرب الشجر ليتحات ورقه فنأكله. والقسي جمع قوس.
قوله: “حتى قرحت أشداقنا”: أي تجرحت من خشونة الورق وحرارته.
وقوله: “ننعشه”: أي نرفعه ونقيمه من شدة الضعف والجهد.
قوله: “واديًا أفيح”: أي واسعًا.
قوله: “كالبعير المخشوش”: هو الذي يجعل في أنفه خشاش، وهو عود يجعل في أنف البعير إذا كان صعبًا، ويشد فيه حبل ليذل وينقاد.
قوله: “بالمنصف”: هو نصف المسافة.
قوله: “فخرجت أحضر”: أي أعدو وأسعى سعيًا شديدًا.
قوله: “فحانت مني لفتة”: اللفتة النظرة إلى جنب.
قوله: “وحسرته”: أي أحددته.
قوله: “فانذلق”: أي صار حادًا.
قوله: “أن يرفه عنهما”: أي يخفف.
قوله: “في أشجاب له”: الأشجاب جمع شجب، وهو السقاء الذي قد أخلق وبلي وصار شنًا.
قوله: “حمارة”: هي أعواد تعلق عليها أسقية الماء.
قوله: “عزلاء”: هي فم القربة.
قوله: “لشربه يابسه”: معناه أنه قليل جدًا.
قوله: “ويغمزه بيديه”: أي يعصره.
قوله: “سيف البحر”: أي ساحله.
قوله: “فزخر البحر”: أي علا موجه.
قوله: “فأورينا”: أي أوقدنا.
قوله: “حجاج عينها”: هو عظمها المستدير بها.
قوله: “وأعظم كفل”: المراد بالكفل هنا الكساء الذي يحويه راكب البعير على سنامه لئلا يسقط، فيحفظ الكفل الراكب.
15118 — ʿAbbād ibn al-Walīd ibn ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit narrated:
My father and I went out seeking knowledge among this clan of the Anṣār before they passed away.
The first person we met was Abū al-Yasar, a Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
With him was a servant boy carrying a bundle of written sheets. Abū al-Yasar was wearing a cloak and a Maʿāfirī garment, and his servant was likewise wearing a cloak and a Maʿāfirī garment.
My father said to him:
“Uncle, I can see signs of anger on your face.”
He replied:
“Indeed. So-and-so, son of so-and-so from Banū Ḥarām, owed me some money. I went to his family, greeted them, and asked, ‘Is he here?’ They replied, ‘No.’ Then a young son of his who was nearing puberty came out to me.
I asked him, ‘Where is your father?’
He replied, ‘He heard your voice and went into my mother’s enclosed room.’
So I called out, ‘Come out to me, for I know where you are.’
He came out, and I asked, ‘What made you hide from me?’
He said, ‘By Allah, I will tell you the truth and not lie to you. By Allah, I feared that I might speak to you and lie, or make you a promise and then break it. You were a Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and by Allah, I am in financial hardship.’
I said, ‘By Allah?’
He said, ‘By Allah.’
I asked again, ‘By Allah?’
He replied, ‘By Allah.’
I asked a third time, ‘By Allah?’
He replied, ‘By Allah.’”
Abū al-Yasar then brought the written document of the debt and erased it with his own hand.
He said:
“If you later become able to repay, then repay me. Otherwise, you are released from it. I testify by these two eyes of mine”—and he placed his fingers upon his eyes—“and these two ears of mine, and this heart of mine that retained it”—and he pointed to his heart—“that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
‘Whoever gives respite to a debtor in hardship, or remits his debt, Allah will shade him in His shade.’”
I said to him:
“Uncle, why do you not take your servant’s cloak and give him your Maʿāfirī garment, then take his Maʿāfirī garment and give him your cloak, so that each of you would have a matching set of garments?”
He wiped my head and said:
“O Allah, bless him.”
Then he said:
“My nephew, these two eyes of mine saw, these two ears of mine heard, and this heart of mine retained”—and he pointed to his heart—“the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saying:
‘Feed them from what you yourselves eat, and clothe them from what you yourselves wear.’”
He continued:
“Giving him some of the possessions of this world is easier for me than having him take from my good deeds on the Day of Resurrection.”
Then we continued until we came to Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh in his mosque.
He was praying wrapped in a single garment.
I stepped past the people and sat between him and the qiblah.
I said:
“May Allah have mercy on you. Are you praying in a single garment while your outer cloak is lying beside you?”
He placed his hand upon my chest like this, spreading and bending his fingers, and said:
“I wanted a foolish person like you to come in, see how I do it, and then do the same.”
Jābir continued:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us in this very mosque carrying a date-palm stalk from Ibn Ṭāb.
He saw some phlegm on the qiblah wall of the mosque and scraped it away with the stalk.
Then he turned toward us and said:
“Which of you would like Allah to turn away from him?”
We became subdued and silent.
He repeated:
“Which of you would like Allah to turn away from him?”
We remained subdued.
He asked a third time:
“Which of you would like Allah to turn away from him?”
We said:
“None of us, O Messenger of Allah.”
He said:
“When one of you stands to pray, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is before his face. So let him not spit in front of himself or to his right. Let him spit to his left beneath his left foot. If something suddenly overcomes him, then let him do this with his garment.”
He then folded part of his garment over another part.
Then he said:
“Bring me some perfume.”
A young man from the neighborhood hurried to his family and returned with some khalūq perfume in his palm.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took it, placed it on the tip of the palm stalk, and smeared it over the place where the phlegm had been.
Jābir said:
“From that incident came your practice of placing perfume in your mosques.”
We traveled with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the expedition of Baṭn Buwāṭ, while he was seeking al-Majdī ibn ʿAmr al-Juhanī.
Five, six, or seven of us would take turns riding a single camel used for carrying water.
When the turn of a man from the Anṣār came to ride his camel, he made it kneel, mounted it, and urged it forward.
The camel hesitated somewhat, so the man said:
“Move! May Allah curse you.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked:
“Who is this person cursing his camel?”
The man replied:
“It is me, O Messenger of Allah.”
He said:
“Get down from it. Do not accompany us with an animal that has been cursed. Do not supplicate against yourselves, do not supplicate against your children, and do not supplicate against your wealth, lest you happen to coincide with a time in which Allah is asked for something and He answers you.”
We continued traveling with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until late afternoon, when we approached a watering place belonging to some Arabs.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Who will go ahead of us, plaster the watering trough, drink, and prepare water for us?”
Jābir said:
I stood and said:
“Here is a man, O Messenger of Allah.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked:
“Who will go with Jābir?”
Jabbār ibn Ṣakhr stood up.
We went to the well, drew one or two buckets of water into the trough, then plastered and repaired it.
We continued drawing water until we filled it completely.
The first person to arrive was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He asked:
“Do you give permission?”
We replied:
“Yes, O Messenger of Allah.”
He lowered his she-camel’s head into the water and she drank.
He then pulled up her reins; she spread her legs and urinated.
He moved her aside and made her kneel.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to the trough and performed wuḍūʾ from it.
I stood and performed wuḍūʾ from the remaining water from the ablution of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
Jabbār ibn Ṣakhr went away to relieve himself.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood to pray.
I was wearing a cloak and tried to cross its two ends over my shoulders, but it was too short.
It had loose hanging ends, so I turned it around, crossed its two ends, and bent my neck down to hold it in place.
Then I came and stood on the left side of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He took me by the hand, moved me around, and placed me on his right.
Then Jabbār ibn Ṣakhr returned, performed wuḍūʾ, and stood on the left side of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took both of us by the hands and moved us backward until he placed us behind him.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept glancing toward me, though at first I did not notice.
Then I became aware of him.
He gestured with his hand, meaning:
“Tighten it around your waist.”
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished the prayer, he said:
“O Jābir.”
I replied:
“At your service, O Messenger of Allah.”
He said:
“If the garment is wide, cross its two ends over your shoulders. If it is narrow, fasten it around your waist.”
We continued traveling with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
The daily provision of each one of us was a single date.
A man would suck on it and then wrap it up in his garment.
We would also strike the trees with our bows so that their leaves fell, and we would eat them, until the sides of our mouths became ulcerated.
One day, by Allah, one of our men was mistakenly not given his date.
We carried him along, supporting him because of his weakness, and testified that he had not received it.
So he was given his date, whereupon he stood up and took it.
We continued traveling with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until we reached a broad valley.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went away to relieve himself, and I followed him carrying a small vessel of water.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked around but saw nothing behind which he could conceal himself.
There were two trees on the edge of the valley.
He went to one of them, took hold of one of its branches, and said:
“Come with me by the permission of Allah.”
It moved along with him like a camel with a nose-peg that submits to its handler.
He then came to the other tree, took one of its branches, and said:
“Come with me by the permission of Allah.”
It moved along with him in the same way.
When he reached the midpoint between the two trees, he brought them together and said:
“Join together over me by the permission of Allah.”
And the two trees joined together.
Jābir said:
I hurried away because I feared that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ might become aware of how close I was and move even farther away. Muḥammad ibn ʿAbbād’s wording has: “move farther away.”
I sat speaking to myself.
Then I happened to glance over and saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ approaching.
The two trees had separated again, each standing upon its own trunk.
I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stop briefly and move his head like this—Abū Ismāʿīl gestured with his head to the right and left—then he continued toward me.
When he reached me, he said:
“O Jābir, did you see where I was standing?”
I replied:
“Yes, O Messenger of Allah.”
He said:
“Go to the two trees and cut a branch from each one. Bring them back, and when you reach the place where I stood, place one branch on your right and one branch on your left.”
Jābir said:
I stood up, took a stone, broke it and sharpened it until it had a cutting edge.
I went to the two trees, cut a branch from each, and dragged them back until I reached the place where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had stood.
I placed one branch on my right and the other on my left.
Then I caught up with him and said:
“I have done it, O Messenger of Allah. Why did you ask me to do that?”
He replied:
“I passed by two graves whose occupants are being punished, and I wished, through my intercession, that their punishment might be lightened for as long as the two branches remain fresh.”
We returned to the camp.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“O Jābir, call out for water for ablution.”
I called:
“Is there any water for ablution? Any water for ablution? Any water for ablution?”
Then I said:
“O Messenger of Allah, I could not find a single drop among the travelers.”
There was a man from the Anṣār who used to cool water for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in worn waterskins hung upon a wooden frame.
The Prophet ﷺ said to me:
“Go to so-and-so, son of so-and-so, the Anṣārī, and see whether there is anything in his waterskins.”
I went and checked them.
I found only a single drop remaining at the mouth of one worn waterskin—so little that if I poured it out, the dry skin itself would absorb it.
I returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said:
“O Messenger of Allah, I found only one drop at the mouth of one waterskin. If I poured it out, the dry waterskin itself would absorb it.”
He said:
“Go and bring it to me.”
I brought it to him.
He took it in his hand, began saying something that I could not understand, and squeezed it with his hands.
Then he gave it back to me and said:
“O Jābir, call for a large basin.”
I called out:
“Bring the travelers’ basin!”
It was brought, carried by several people, and I placed it before him.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ spread his hand in the basin, separated his fingers, and placed his hand at the bottom of it.
Then he said:
“Take it, O Jābir. Pour over my hand and say: ‘In the name of Allah.’”
I poured and said:
“In the name of Allah.”
Then I saw water bursting forth from between the fingers of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
The basin began filling and swirling with water until it became full.
He said:
“O Jābir, call everyone who needs water.”
The people came and drew water until they were completely satisfied.
I asked:
“Is there anyone left who still needs water?”
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ lifted his hand from the basin while it was still full.
The people complained of hunger to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He said:
“Perhaps Allah will feed you.”
We came to the seashore.
The sea surged strongly and cast out a huge sea creature.
We lit a fire beside it, cooked and roasted from it, and ate until we were full.
Jābir said:
Five of us, including myself and several others whom he named, entered into the socket of its eye without anyone outside being able to see us.
Then we came out and took one of its ribs and stood it upright like an arch.
We called for the tallest man among the travelers, the largest camel among them, and the largest riding cushion among them.
The rider passed beneath that rib without even needing to lower his head.
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (3006–3014).
Explanation of Uncommon Words
The phrase “with him was a ḍamāmah of written sheets” means a bundle of sheets gathered together.
A burdah is a striped wrap or cloak.
A Maʿāfirī garment is a type of clothing manufactured in a place called Maʿāfir.
“Safʿah of anger” means a visible sign or change in the face caused by anger.
A jafr is a young boy approaching puberty.
“Manāṭ qalbihi” refers to the part or vessel attached to the heart.
A ḥullah consists of a lower garment and an upper cloak.
An ʿurjūn is a palm stalk or branch.
Ibn Ṭāb is a type of date.
Regarding “ʿabīr,” Abū ʿUbayd said that it means saffron alone, while al-Aṣmaʿī said it is a mixture of perfumes combined with saffron.
Khalūq is a perfume composed of several fragrances mixed with saffron; according to al-Aṣmaʿī, this is what is meant by ʿabīr.
Baṭn Buwāṭ is a mountain in the territory of Juhaynah.
A nāḍiḥ is a camel used for drawing water.
The phrase “shaʾ, may Allah curse you” contains shaʾ, a word used to drive or rebuke a camel.
“Yamdur al-ḥawḍ” means to plaster the trough with mud and repair it.
“Until we afhaqnāhu” means until we filled it completely.
“He caused his she-camel to drink” means that he lowered her head into the water.
“Shanaqa lahā” means that he restrained her with the reins while mounted.
“Fashajat” means that the camel spread its legs apart in order to urinate.
Dhadhābhib are loose hanging ends of a garment. The singular is dhubdhub. They are so called because they sway and move as the wearer walks.
“Fanakkastuhā” means “I turned it upside down.” From the same root comes the description of a breech birth, when the feet emerge before the head.
“Tawāqaṣtu ʿalayhā” means that he held the garment in place with his neck, bending over it so that it would not fall.
“Fasten it around your ḥaqw” refers to the place where the lower garment is tied, here meaning around the level of the waist or navel.
“We used to nakhtabiṭ with our bows” means that they struck trees with their bows so that the leaves would fall and they could eat them. Qisiyy is the plural of bow.
“Until our ashdaq became ulcerated” means that the sides of their mouths became wounded because of the roughness and harshness of the leaves.
“We supported him” means that they lifted and steadied him because of his severe weakness and exhaustion.
An afyaḥ valley means a broad and spacious valley.
A mukhshūsh camel is one with a small wooden peg placed through its nose when it is difficult to control, with a rope attached to it so that it becomes submissive and manageable.
“At the munṣaf” means at the halfway point.
“I went away quickly” means that he ran rapidly.
“A glance occurred from me” means that he looked to the side.
“Wa-ḥasartuhu” means that he sharpened it.
“Fa-indhalaqa” means that it became sharp.
“That relief be given to them” means that their punishment be lightened.
Ashjāb is the plural of shajb, meaning an old worn waterskin that has become thin and weathered.
A ḥimārah here means a wooden frame upon which waterskins are hung.
ʿAzlāʾ means the mouth or opening of a waterskin.
The phrase means that the amount of water was so tiny that the dry waterskin itself would absorb it.
“He squeezed it with his hands” means that he pressed and wrung it.
Sayf al-baḥr means the seashore.
“The sea surged” means that its waves rose.
“Fa-awraynā” means “we kindled a fire.”
The ḥijāj of its eye is the circular bone surrounding the eye socket.
The largest kifl here means the cloth or padding arranged by a camel rider over the hump to prevent himself from falling; it supports and secures the rider.

١٥١١٨ — عن عباد بن الوليد بن عبادة بن الصامت قال: خرجت أنا وأبي نطلب العلم في هذا الحي من الأنصار قبل أن يهلكوا، فكان أول من لقينا أبا اليسر صاحب رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، ومعه غلام له، معه ضمامة من صحف، وعلى أبي اليسر بردة ومعافري، وعلى غلامه بردة ومعافري، فقال له أبي: يا عم، إني أرى في وجهك سفعة من غضب. قال: أجل، كان لي على فلان بن فلان الحرامي مال، فأتيت أهله فسلمت، فقلت: ثم هو؟ قالوا: لا. فخرج علي ابن له جفر، فقلت له: أين أبوك؟ قال: سمع صوتك فدخل أريكة أمي. فقلت: اخرج إلي، فقد علمت أين أنت. فخرج، فقلت: ما حملك على أن اختبأت مني؟ قال: أنا واللّٰه أحدثك ثم لا أكذبك، خشيت واللّٰه أن أحدثك فأكذبك، وأن أعدك فأخلفك، وكنت صاحب رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، وكنت واللّٰه معسرًا. قال قلت: آللّٰه؟ قال: اللّٰه. قلت: آللّٰه؟ قال: اللّٰه. قلت: آللّٰه؟ قال: اللّٰه. قال: فأتى بصحيفته فمحاها بيده، فقال: إن وجدت قضاء فاقضني، وإلا أنت في حل، فأشهد بصر عيني هاتين - ووضع إصبعيه على عينيه - وسمع أذني هاتين، ووعاه قلبي هذا - وأشار إلى مناط قلبه - رسول اللّٰه ﷺ وهو يقول:
((من أنظر معسرًا، أو وضع عنه، أظله اللّٰه في ظله)).
قال: فقلت له أنا: يا عم، لو أنك أخذت بردة غلامك وأعطيته معافريك، وأخذت معافريه وأعطيته بردتك، فكانت عليك حلة وعليه حلة. فمسح رأسي وقال: اللهم بارك فيه. يا ابن أخي، بصر عيني هاتين، وسمع أذني هاتين، ووعاه قلبي هذا - وأشار إلى مناط قلبه - رسول اللّٰه ﷺ وهو يقول:
((أطعموهم مما تأكلون، وألبسوهم مما تلبسون)).
وكان أن أعطيه من متاع الدنيا أهون علي من أن يأخذ من حسناتي يوم القيامة.
ثم مضينا حتى أتينا جابر بن عبد اللّٰه في مسجده، وهو يصلي في ثوب واحد مشتملًا به، فتخطيت القوم حتى جلست بينه وبين القبلة، فقلت: يرحمك اللّٰه، أتصلي في ثوب واحد ورداؤك إلى جنبك؟ قال: فقال بيده في صدري هكذا، وفرق بين أصابعه وقوسها: أردت أن يدخل علي الأحمق مثلك، فيراني كيف أصنع، فيصنع مثله.
أتانا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ في مسجدنا هذا، وفي يده عرجون ابن طاب، فرأى في قبلة المسجد نخامة فحكها بالعرجون، ثم أقبل علينا فقال:
((أيكم يحب أن يعرض اللّٰه عنه؟)).
قال: فخشعنا، ثم قال:
((أيكم يحب أن يعرض اللّٰه عنه؟)).
قال: فخشعنا، ثم قال:
((أيكم يحب أن يعرض اللّٰه عنه؟)).
قلنا: لا أينا يا رسول اللّٰه! قال:
((فإن أحدكم إذا قام يصلي، فإن اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى قبل وجهه، فلا يبصقن قبل وجهه، ولا عن يمينه، وليبصق عن يساره تحت رجله اليسرى، فإن عجلت به بادرة، فليقل بثوبه هكذا)).
ثم طوى ثوبه بعضه على بعض، فقال:
((أروني عبيرًا)).
فقام فتى من الحي يشتد إلى أهله، فجاء بخلوق في راحته، فأخذه رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فجعله على رأس العرجون، ثم لطخ به على أثر النخامة.
فقال جابر: فمن هناك جعلتم الخلوق في مساجدكم.
سرنا مع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ في غزوة بطن بواط، وهو يطلب المجدي بن عمرو الجهني، وكان الناضح يعقبه منا الخمسة والستة والسبعة، فدارت عقبة رجل من الأنصار على ناضح له، فأناخه فركبه، ثم بعثه فتلدن عليه بعض التلدن، فقال له: شأ، لعنك اللّٰه. فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((من هذا اللاعن بعيره؟)).
قال: أنا يا رسول اللّٰه. قال:
((انزل عنه، فلا تصحبنا بملعون، لا تدعوا على أنفسكم، ولا تدعوا على أولادكم، ولا تدعوا على أموالكم، لا توافقوا من اللّٰه ساعة يسأل فيها عطاء، فيستجيب لكم)).
سرنا مع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ حتى إذا كانت عشيشية ودنونا ماء من مياه العرب، قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((من رجل يتقدمنا فيمدر الحوض فيشرب ويسقينا؟)).
قال جابر: فقمت، فقلت: هذا رجل يا رسول اللّٰه. فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((أي رجل مع جابر؟)).
فقام جبار بن صخر، فانطلقنا إلى البئر، فنزعنا في الحوض سجلًا أو سجلين، ثم مدرناه، ثم نزعنا فيه حتى أَفْهَقْناه، فكان أول طالع علينا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فقال:
((أتأذنان؟)).
قلنا: نعم يا رسول اللّٰه. فأشرع ناقته فشربت، شنق لها فشجت فبالت، ثم عدل بها فأناخها، ثم جاء رسول اللّٰه ﷺ إلى الحوض فتوضأ منه، ثم قمت فتوضأت من متوضأ رسول اللّٰه ﷺ.
فذهب جبار بن صخر يقضي حاجته، فقام رسول اللّٰه ﷺ ليصلي، وكانت علي بردة، ذهبت أن أخالف بين طرفيها فلم تبلغ لي، وكانت لها ذباذب، فنكستها، ثم خالفت بين طرفيها، ثم تواقصت عليها، ثم جئت حتى قمت عن يسار رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فأخذ بيدي فأدارني حتى أقامني عن يمينه، ثم جاء جبار بن صخر فتوضأ، ثم جاء فقام عن يسار رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فأخذ رسول اللّٰه ﷺ بيدينا جميعًا، فدفعنا حتى أقامنا خلفه، فجعل رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يرمقني وأنا لا أشعر، ثم فطنت به، فقال هكذا بيده، يعني: شد وسطك. فلما فرغ رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قال:
((يا جابر)).
قلت: لبيك يا رسول اللّٰه. قال:
((إذا كان واسعًا فخالف بين طرفيه، وإذا كان ضيقًا فاشدده على حقوك)).
سرنا مع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، وكان قوت كل رجل منا في كل يوم تمرة، فكان يمصها ثم يصرها في ثوبه، وكنا نختبط بقسينا ونأكل، حتى قرحت أشداقنا، فأقسم أخطئها رجل منا يومًا، فانطلقنا به ننعشه، فشهدنا أنه لم يعطها، فأعطيها فقام فأخذها.
سرنا مع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ حتى نزلنا واديًا أفيح، فذهب رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يقضي حاجته، فاتبعته بإداوة من ماء، فنظر رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فلم ير شيئًا يستتر به، فإذا شجرتان بشاطئ الوادي، فانطلق رسول اللّٰه ﷺ إلى إحداهما فأخذ بغصن من أغصانها، فقال:
((انقادي علي بإذن اللّٰه)).
فانقادت معه كالبعير المخشوش الذي يصانع قائده، حتى أتى الشجرة الأخرى، فأخذ بغصن من أغصانها، فقال:
((انقادي علي بإذن اللّٰه)).
فانقادت معه كذلك، حتى إذا كان بالمنصف مما بينهما، لأم بينهما - يعني جمعهما - فقال:
((التئما علي بإذن اللّٰه)).
فالتأمتا.
قال جابر: فخرجت أحضر مخافة أن يحس رسول اللّٰه ﷺ بقربي فيبتعد، (وقال محمد بن عباد: فيتبعد)، فجلست أحدث نفسي، فحانت مني لفتة، فإذا أنا برسول اللّٰه ﷺ مقبلًا، وإذا الشجرتان قد افترقتا، فقامت كل واحدة منهما على ساق، فرأيت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ وقف وقفة، فقال برأسه هكذا - وأشار أبو إسماعيل برأسه يمينًا وشمالًا - ثم أقبل. فلما انتهى إلي قال:
((يا جابر، هل رأيت مقامي؟)).
قلت: نعم يا رسول اللّٰه. قال:
((فانطلق إلى الشجرتين، فاقطع من كل واحدة منهما غصنًا، فأقبل بهما، حتى إذا قمت مقامي فأرسل غصنًا عن يمينك وغصنًا عن يسارك)).
قال جابر: فقمت فأخذت حجرًا فكسرته وحسرته، فانذلق لي، فأتيت الشجرتين فقطعت من كل واحدة منهما غصنًا، ثم أقبلت أجرهما حتى قمت مقام رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، أرسلت غصنًا عن يميني وغصنًا عن يساري، ثم لحقته فقلت: قد فعلت يا رسول اللّٰه، فعم ذاك؟ قال:
((إني مررت بقبرين يعذبان، فأحببت بشفاعتي أن يرفه عنهما، ما دام الغصنان رطبين)).
قال: فأتينا العسكر، فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((يا جابر، ناد بوضوء)).
فقلت: ألا وضوء؟ ألا وضوء؟ ألا وضوء؟ قال قلت: يا رسول اللّٰه، ما وجدت في الركب من قطرة. وكان رجل من الأنصار يبرد لرسول اللّٰه ﷺ الماء في أشجاب له على حمارة من جريد، قال: فقال لي:
((انطلق إلى فلان ابن فلان الأنصاري، فانظر هل في أشجابه من شيء؟)).
قال: فانطلقت إليه فنظرت فيها فلم أجد فيها إلا قطرة في عزلاء شجب منها، لو أني أفرغه لشربه يابسه، فأتيت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فقلت: يا رسول اللّٰه، إني لم أجد فيها إلا قطرة في عزلاء شجب منها، لو أني أفرغه لشربه يابسه. قال:
((اذهب فأتني به)).
فأتيته به، فأخذه بيده فجعل يتكلم بشيء لا أدري ما هو، ويغمزه بيديه، ثم أعطانيه فقال:
((يا جابر، ناد بجفنة)).
فقلت: يا جفنة الركب! فأُتيت بها تُحمل، فوضعتها بين يديه، فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ بيده في الجفنة هكذا، فبسطها وفرق بين أصابعه، ثم وضعها في قعر الجفنة، وقال:
((خذ يا جابر، فصب علي، وقل: باسم اللّٰه)).
فصببت عليه وقلت: باسم اللّٰه، فرأيت الماء يفور من بين أصابع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، ثم فارت الجفنة ودارت حتى امتلأت، فقال:
((يا جابر، ناد من كان له حاجة بماء)).
قال: فأتى الناس فاستقوا حتى رووا، قال فقلت: هل بقي أحد له حاجة؟ فرفع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يده من الجفنة وهي ملأى.
وشكا الناس إلى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ الجوع، فقال:
((عسى اللّٰه أن يطعمكم)).
فأتينا سيف البحر، فزخر البحر زخرة، فألقى دابة، فأورينا على شقها النار، فاطبخنا واشتوينا وأكلنا حتى شبعنا. قال جابر: فدخلت أنا وفلان وفلان، حتى عد خمسة، في حجاج عينها، ما يرانا أحد، حتى خرجنا، فأخذنا ضلعًا من أضلاعها فقوسناه، ثم دعونا بأعظم رجل في الركب، وأعظم جمل في الركب، وأعظم كفل في الركب، فدخل تحته ما يطأطئ رأسه.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٣٠٠٦-٣٠١٤).
شرح الكلمات الغريبة
قوله: “معه ضمامة من صحف”: أي رزمة يضم بعضها إلى بعض.
قوله: “بردة”: وهي شملة مخططة.
قوله: “معافري”: نوع من الثياب يعمل بقرية تسمى معافر.
قوله: “سفعة من غضب”: علامة وتغير.
قوله: “جفر”: هو الذي قارب البلوغ.
قوله: “مناط قلبه”: هو عرق معلق بالقلب.
قوله: “حلة”: هي إزار ورداء.
قوله: “عرجون”: هو الغصن.
قوله: “ابن طاب”: نوع من التمر.
قوله: “عبيرًا”: قال أبو عبيد: هو الزعفران وحده. وقال الأصمعي: هو أخلاط من الطيب تجمع بالزعفران.
قوله: “بخلوق”: هو طيب من أنواع مختلفة يجمع بالزعفران، وهو العبير كما قال الأصمعي.
قوله: “بطن بواط”: هو جبل من جبال جهينة.
قوله: “الناضح”: أي البعير الذي يستقى عليه.
قوله: “شأ لعنك اللّٰه”: هي كلمة زجر للبعير، يقال: شأشأت البعير إذا زجرته وقلت له: شأ.
قوله: “فيمدر الحوض”: أي يطينه ويصلحه.
قوله: “حتى أفهقناه”: أي ملأناه.
قوله: “فأشرع ناقته”: أرسل رأسها في الماء لتشرب.
قوله: “شنق لها”: يقال: شنقها وأشنقها أي كففها بزمامها وأنت راكبها.
قوله: “فشجت”: يقال: فشج البعير إذا فرج بين رجليه للبول.
قوله: “ذباذب”: واحدها ذبذب، سميت بذلك لأنها تتذبذب على صاحبها إذا مشى - أي أنها تتحرك وتضطرب -.
قوله: “فنكستها”: أي قلبته، ومنه قيل: ولد منكوس، إذا خرج رجلاه قبل رأسه.
قوله: “تواقصت عليها”: أي أمسكت عليها بعنقي وحنيته عليها لئلا تسقط.
قوله: “فاشدده على حقوك”: هو معقد الإزار، المراد هنا: أن يبلغ السرة.
قوله: “وكنا نختبط بقسينا”: معنى نختبط نضرب الشجر ليتحات ورقه فنأكله. والقسي جمع قوس.
قوله: “حتى قرحت أشداقنا”: أي تجرحت من خشونة الورق وحرارته.
وقوله: “ننعشه”: أي نرفعه ونقيمه من شدة الضعف والجهد.
قوله: “واديًا أفيح”: أي واسعًا.
قوله: “كالبعير المخشوش”: هو الذي يجعل في أنفه خشاش، وهو عود يجعل في أنف البعير إذا كان صعبًا، ويشد فيه حبل ليذل وينقاد.
قوله: “بالمنصف”: هو نصف المسافة.
قوله: “فخرجت أحضر”: أي أعدو وأسعى سعيًا شديدًا.
قوله: “فحانت مني لفتة”: اللفتة النظرة إلى جنب.
قوله: “وحسرته”: أي أحددته.
قوله: “فانذلق”: أي صار حادًا.
قوله: “أن يرفه عنهما”: أي يخفف.
قوله: “في أشجاب له”: الأشجاب جمع شجب، وهو السقاء الذي قد أخلق وبلي وصار شنًا.
قوله: “حمارة”: هي أعواد تعلق عليها أسقية الماء.
قوله: “عزلاء”: هي فم القربة.
قوله: “لشربه يابسه”: معناه أنه قليل جدًا.
قوله: “ويغمزه بيديه”: أي يعصره.
قوله: “سيف البحر”: أي ساحله.
قوله: “فزخر البحر”: أي علا موجه.
قوله: “فأورينا”: أي أوقدنا.
قوله: “حجاج عينها”: هو عظمها المستدير بها.
قوله: “وأعظم كفل”: المراد بالكفل هنا الكساء الذي يحويه راكب البعير على سنامه لئلا يسقط، فيحفظ الكفل الراكب.
15118 — ʿAbbād ibn al-Walīd ibn ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit narrated:
My father and I went out seeking knowledge among this clan of the Anṣār before they passed away.
The first person we met was Abū al-Yasar, a Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
With him was a servant boy carrying a bundle of written sheets. Abū al-Yasar was wearing a cloak and a Maʿāfirī garment, and his servant was likewise wearing a cloak and a Maʿāfirī garment.
My father said to him:
“Uncle, I can see signs of anger on your face.”
He replied:
“Indeed. So-and-so, son of so-and-so from Banū Ḥarām, owed me some money. I went to his family, greeted them, and asked, ‘Is he here?’ They replied, ‘No.’ Then a young son of his who was nearing puberty came out to me.
I asked him, ‘Where is your father?’
He replied, ‘He heard your voice and went into my mother’s enclosed room.’
So I called out, ‘Come out to me, for I know where you are.’
He came out, and I asked, ‘What made you hide from me?’
He said, ‘By Allah, I will tell you the truth and not lie to you. By Allah, I feared that I might speak to you and lie, or make you a promise and then break it. You were a Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and by Allah, I am in financial hardship.’
I said, ‘By Allah?’
He said, ‘By Allah.’
I asked again, ‘By Allah?’
He replied, ‘By Allah.’
I asked a third time, ‘By Allah?’
He replied, ‘By Allah.’”
Abū al-Yasar then brought the written document of the debt and erased it with his own hand.
He said:
“If you later become able to repay, then repay me. Otherwise, you are released from it. I testify by these two eyes of mine”—and he placed his fingers upon his eyes—“and these two ears of mine, and this heart of mine that retained it”—and he pointed to his heart—“that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
‘Whoever gives respite to a debtor in hardship, or remits his debt, Allah will shade him in His shade.’”
I said to him:
“Uncle, why do you not take your servant’s cloak and give him your Maʿāfirī garment, then take his Maʿāfirī garment and give him your cloak, so that each of you would have a matching set of garments?”
He wiped my head and said:
“O Allah, bless him.”
Then he said:
“My nephew, these two eyes of mine saw, these two ears of mine heard, and this heart of mine retained”—and he pointed to his heart—“the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saying:
‘Feed them from what you yourselves eat, and clothe them from what you yourselves wear.’”
He continued:
“Giving him some of the possessions of this world is easier for me than having him take from my good deeds on the Day of Resurrection.”
Then we continued until we came to Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh in his mosque.
He was praying wrapped in a single garment.
I stepped past the people and sat between him and the qiblah.
I said:
“May Allah have mercy on you. Are you praying in a single garment while your outer cloak is lying beside you?”
He placed his hand upon my chest like this, spreading and bending his fingers, and said:
“I wanted a foolish person like you to come in, see how I do it, and then do the same.”
Jābir continued:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us in this very mosque carrying a date-palm stalk from Ibn Ṭāb.
He saw some phlegm on the qiblah wall of the mosque and scraped it away with the stalk.
Then he turned toward us and said:
“Which of you would like Allah to turn away from him?”
We became subdued and silent.
He repeated:
“Which of you would like Allah to turn away from him?”
We remained subdued.
He asked a third time:
“Which of you would like Allah to turn away from him?”
We said:
“None of us, O Messenger of Allah.”
He said:
“When one of you stands to pray, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is before his face. So let him not spit in front of himself or to his right. Let him spit to his left beneath his left foot. If something suddenly overcomes him, then let him do this with his garment.”
He then folded part of his garment over another part.
Then he said:
“Bring me some perfume.”
A young man from the neighborhood hurried to his family and returned with some khalūq perfume in his palm.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took it, placed it on the tip of the palm stalk, and smeared it over the place where the phlegm had been.
Jābir said:
“From that incident came your practice of placing perfume in your mosques.”
We traveled with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the expedition of Baṭn Buwāṭ, while he was seeking al-Majdī ibn ʿAmr al-Juhanī.
Five, six, or seven of us would take turns riding a single camel used for carrying water.
When the turn of a man from the Anṣār came to ride his camel, he made it kneel, mounted it, and urged it forward.
The camel hesitated somewhat, so the man said:
“Move! May Allah curse you.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked:
“Who is this person cursing his camel?”
The man replied:
“It is me, O Messenger of Allah.”
He said:
“Get down from it. Do not accompany us with an animal that has been cursed. Do not supplicate against yourselves, do not supplicate against your children, and do not supplicate against your wealth, lest you happen to coincide with a time in which Allah is asked for something and He answers you.”
We continued traveling with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until late afternoon, when we approached a watering place belonging to some Arabs.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Who will go ahead of us, plaster the watering trough, drink, and prepare water for us?”
Jābir said:
I stood and said:
“Here is a man, O Messenger of Allah.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked:
“Who will go with Jābir?”
Jabbār ibn Ṣakhr stood up.
We went to the well, drew one or two buckets of water into the trough, then plastered and repaired it.
We continued drawing water until we filled it completely.
The first person to arrive was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He asked:
“Do you give permission?”
We replied:
“Yes, O Messenger of Allah.”
He lowered his she-camel’s head into the water and she drank.
He then pulled up her reins; she spread her legs and urinated.
He moved her aside and made her kneel.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to the trough and performed wuḍūʾ from it.
I stood and performed wuḍūʾ from the remaining water from the ablution of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
Jabbār ibn Ṣakhr went away to relieve himself.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood to pray.
I was wearing a cloak and tried to cross its two ends over my shoulders, but it was too short.
It had loose hanging ends, so I turned it around, crossed its two ends, and bent my neck down to hold it in place.
Then I came and stood on the left side of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He took me by the hand, moved me around, and placed me on his right.
Then Jabbār ibn Ṣakhr returned, performed wuḍūʾ, and stood on the left side of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took both of us by the hands and moved us backward until he placed us behind him.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept glancing toward me, though at first I did not notice.
Then I became aware of him.
He gestured with his hand, meaning:
“Tighten it around your waist.”
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished the prayer, he said:
“O Jābir.”
I replied:
“At your service, O Messenger of Allah.”
He said:
“If the garment is wide, cross its two ends over your shoulders. If it is narrow, fasten it around your waist.”
We continued traveling with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
The daily provision of each one of us was a single date.
A man would suck on it and then wrap it up in his garment.
We would also strike the trees with our bows so that their leaves fell, and we would eat them, until the sides of our mouths became ulcerated.
One day, by Allah, one of our men was mistakenly not given his date.
We carried him along, supporting him because of his weakness, and testified that he had not received it.
So he was given his date, whereupon he stood up and took it.
We continued traveling with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until we reached a broad valley.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went away to relieve himself, and I followed him carrying a small vessel of water.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked around but saw nothing behind which he could conceal himself.
There were two trees on the edge of the valley.
He went to one of them, took hold of one of its branches, and said:
“Come with me by the permission of Allah.”
It moved along with him like a camel with a nose-peg that submits to its handler.
He then came to the other tree, took one of its branches, and said:
“Come with me by the permission of Allah.”
It moved along with him in the same way.
When he reached the midpoint between the two trees, he brought them together and said:
“Join together over me by the permission of Allah.”
And the two trees joined together.
Jābir said:
I hurried away because I feared that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ might become aware of how close I was and move even farther away. Muḥammad ibn ʿAbbād’s wording has: “move farther away.”
I sat speaking to myself.
Then I happened to glance over and saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ approaching.
The two trees had separated again, each standing upon its own trunk.
I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stop briefly and move his head like this—Abū Ismāʿīl gestured with his head to the right and left—then he continued toward me.
When he reached me, he said:
“O Jābir, did you see where I was standing?”
I replied:
“Yes, O Messenger of Allah.”
He said:
“Go to the two trees and cut a branch from each one. Bring them back, and when you reach the place where I stood, place one branch on your right and one branch on your left.”
Jābir said:
I stood up, took a stone, broke it and sharpened it until it had a cutting edge.
I went to the two trees, cut a branch from each, and dragged them back until I reached the place where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had stood.
I placed one branch on my right and the other on my left.
Then I caught up with him and said:
“I have done it, O Messenger of Allah. Why did you ask me to do that?”
He replied:
“I passed by two graves whose occupants are being punished, and I wished, through my intercession, that their punishment might be lightened for as long as the two branches remain fresh.”
We returned to the camp.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“O Jābir, call out for water for ablution.”
I called:
“Is there any water for ablution? Any water for ablution? Any water for ablution?”
Then I said:
“O Messenger of Allah, I could not find a single drop among the travelers.”
There was a man from the Anṣār who used to cool water for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in worn waterskins hung upon a wooden frame.
The Prophet ﷺ said to me:
“Go to so-and-so, son of so-and-so, the Anṣārī, and see whether there is anything in his waterskins.”
I went and checked them.
I found only a single drop remaining at the mouth of one worn waterskin—so little that if I poured it out, the dry skin itself would absorb it.
I returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said:
“O Messenger of Allah, I found only one drop at the mouth of one waterskin. If I poured it out, the dry waterskin itself would absorb it.”
He said:
“Go and bring it to me.”
I brought it to him.
He took it in his hand, began saying something that I could not understand, and squeezed it with his hands.
Then he gave it back to me and said:
“O Jābir, call for a large basin.”
I called out:
“Bring the travelers’ basin!”
It was brought, carried by several people, and I placed it before him.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ spread his hand in the basin, separated his fingers, and placed his hand at the bottom of it.
Then he said:
“Take it, O Jābir. Pour over my hand and say: ‘In the name of Allah.’”
I poured and said:
“In the name of Allah.”
Then I saw water bursting forth from between the fingers of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
The basin began filling and swirling with water until it became full.
He said:
“O Jābir, call everyone who needs water.”
The people came and drew water until they were completely satisfied.
I asked:
“Is there anyone left who still needs water?”
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ lifted his hand from the basin while it was still full.
The people complained of hunger to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He said:
“Perhaps Allah will feed you.”
We came to the seashore.
The sea surged strongly and cast out a huge sea creature.
We lit a fire beside it, cooked and roasted from it, and ate until we were full.
Jābir said:
Five of us, including myself and several others whom he named, entered into the socket of its eye without anyone outside being able to see us.
Then we came out and took one of its ribs and stood it upright like an arch.
We called for the tallest man among the travelers, the largest camel among them, and the largest riding cushion among them.
The rider passed beneath that rib without even needing to lower his head.
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (3006–3014).
Explanation of Uncommon Words
The phrase “with him was a ḍamāmah of written sheets” means a bundle of sheets gathered together.
A burdah is a striped wrap or cloak.
A Maʿāfirī garment is a type of clothing manufactured in a place called Maʿāfir.
“Safʿah of anger” means a visible sign or change in the face caused by anger.
A jafr is a young boy approaching puberty.
“Manāṭ qalbihi” refers to the part or vessel attached to the heart.
A ḥullah consists of a lower garment and an upper cloak.
An ʿurjūn is a palm stalk or branch.
Ibn Ṭāb is a type of date.
Regarding “ʿabīr,” Abū ʿUbayd said that it means saffron alone, while al-Aṣmaʿī said it is a mixture of perfumes combined with saffron.
Khalūq is a perfume composed of several fragrances mixed with saffron; according to al-Aṣmaʿī, this is what is meant by ʿabīr.
Baṭn Buwāṭ is a mountain in the territory of Juhaynah.
A nāḍiḥ is a camel used for drawing water.
The phrase “shaʾ, may Allah curse you” contains shaʾ, a word used to drive or rebuke a camel.
“Yamdur al-ḥawḍ” means to plaster the trough with mud and repair it.
“Until we afhaqnāhu” means until we filled it completely.
“He caused his she-camel to drink” means that he lowered her head into the water.
“Shanaqa lahā” means that he restrained her with the reins while mounted.
“Fashajat” means that the camel spread its legs apart in order to urinate.
Dhadhābhib are loose hanging ends of a garment. The singular is dhubdhub. They are so called because they sway and move as the wearer walks.
“Fanakkastuhā” means “I turned it upside down.” From the same root comes the description of a breech birth, when the feet emerge before the head.
“Tawāqaṣtu ʿalayhā” means that he held the garment in place with his neck, bending over it so that it would not fall.
“Fasten it around your ḥaqw” refers to the place where the lower garment is tied, here meaning around the level of the waist or navel.
“We used to nakhtabiṭ with our bows” means that they struck trees with their bows so that the leaves would fall and they could eat them. Qisiyy is the plural of bow.
“Until our ashdaq became ulcerated” means that the sides of their mouths became wounded because of the roughness and harshness of the leaves.
“We supported him” means that they lifted and steadied him because of his severe weakness and exhaustion.
An afyaḥ valley means a broad and spacious valley.
A mukhshūsh camel is one with a small wooden peg placed through its nose when it is difficult to control, with a rope attached to it so that it becomes submissive and manageable.
“At the munṣaf” means at the halfway point.
“I went away quickly” means that he ran rapidly.
“A glance occurred from me” means that he looked to the side.
“Wa-ḥasartuhu” means that he sharpened it.
“Fa-indhalaqa” means that it became sharp.
“That relief be given to them” means that their punishment be lightened.
Ashjāb is the plural of shajb, meaning an old worn waterskin that has become thin and weathered.
A ḥimārah here means a wooden frame upon which waterskins are hung.
ʿAzlāʾ means the mouth or opening of a waterskin.
The phrase means that the amount of water was so tiny that the dry waterskin itself would absorb it.
“He squeezed it with his hands” means that he pressed and wrung it.
Sayf al-baḥr means the seashore.
“The sea surged” means that its waves rose.
“Fa-awraynā” means “we kindled a fire.”
The ḥijāj of its eye is the circular bone surrounding the eye socket.
The largest kifl here means the cloth or padding arranged by a camel rider over the hump to prevent himself from falling; it supports and secures the rider.

١٥١٢١ — عن سهل بن سعد الساعدي قال: مر رجل على رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فقال لرجل عنده جالس:
((ما رأيك في هذا؟)).
فقال: رجل من أشراف الناس، هذا واللّٰه حري إن خطب أن ينكح، وإن شفع أن يشفع. قال: فسكت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، ثم مر رجل، فقال له رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((ما رأيك في هذا؟)).
فقال: يا رسول اللّٰه، هذا رجل من فقراء المسلمين، هذا حري إن خطب أن لا ينكح، وإن شفع أن لا يشفع، وإن قال أن لا يسمع لقوله. فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((هذا خير من ملء الأرض من مثل هذا)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٦٤٤٧).

15121 — Sahl ibn Saʿd al-Sāʿidī narrated:
A man passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
The Prophet ﷺ asked a man sitting with him:
“What is your opinion of this man?”
He replied:
“He is one of the noble people. By Allah, if he proposes marriage, he deserves to be accepted; and if he intercedes, his intercession deserves to be accepted.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained silent.
Then another man passed by.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked:
“What is your opinion of this man?”
He replied:
“O Messenger of Allah, this is one of the poor Muslims. If he proposes marriage, he is likely not to be accepted; if he intercedes, his intercession is likely not to be accepted; and if he speaks, people are unlikely to listen to him.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“This man is better than an earthful of people like the first man.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6447).

١٥١٢٢ — عن أبي ذر قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((يا أبا ذر، ارفع بصرك فانظر أرفع رجل تراه في المسجد)).
قال: فنظرت، فإذا رجل جالس عليه حلة، قال: فقلت: هذا. قال: فقال:
((يا أبا ذر، ارفع بصرك فانظر أوضع رجل تراه في المسجد)).
قال: فنظرت، فإذا رجل ضعيف عليه أخلاق، قال: فقلت: هذا. قال: فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((والذي نفسي بيده، لهذا أفضل عند اللّٰه يوم القيامة من قراب الأرض مثل هذا)).
صحيح: رواه أحمد (٢١٤٩٣) - واللفظ له -، وابن أبي شيبة (٣٥٤٥٧)، وهناد في الزهد (٨١٥).

15122 — Abū Dharr narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“O Abū Dharr, raise your gaze and look for the most prominent man you can see in the mosque.”
I looked and saw a man seated wearing a fine set of garments.
I said:
“This man.”
He then said:
“O Abū Dharr, raise your gaze and look for the lowest-ranking man you can see in the mosque.”
I looked and saw a weak man wearing worn-out clothes.
I said:
“This man.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“By the One in whose Hand is my soul, this man will be better before Allah on the Day of Resurrection than an earthful of men like that other one.”
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (21493), and this is his wording, Ibn Abī Shaybah (35457), and Hannād in al-Zuhd (815).

١٥١٢٣ — عن أبي ذر أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قال له:
((كيف ترى جعيلاً؟)).
قال: فقلت: مسكينًا شكله من الناس. قال:
((فكيف ترى فلانًا؟)).
قلت: سيدًا من سادات الناس. قال:
((فجعيل خير من ملء الأرض، أو آلاف، أو نحو ذلك من فلان)).
قال: قلت: يا رسول اللّٰه، ففلان هكذا، وأنت تصنع به ما تصنع؟ فقال:
((إنه رأس قومه، فأنا أتألفهم فيه)).
صحيح: رواه ابن وهب في الجامع (٣٤).

15123 — Abū Dharr narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
“What do you think of Juʿayl?”
I replied:
“He is a poor man, like others of his kind among the people.”
He asked:
“And what do you think of so-and-so?”
I replied:
“He is a leader among the leaders of the people.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Juʿayl is better than an earthful—or thousands, or something similar—of men like so-and-so.”
I said:
“O Messenger of Allah, if so-and-so is like that, why do you treat him as you do?”
He replied:
“He is the leader of his people, so through him I seek to win their hearts.”
Authentic: Narrated by Ibn Wahb in al-Jāmiʿ (34).

15123 — Abū Dharr narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
“What do you think of Juʿayl?”
I replied:
“He is a poor man, like others of his kind among the people.”
He asked:
“And what do you think of so-and-so?”
I replied:
“He is a leader among the leaders of the people.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Juʿayl is better than an earthful—or thousands, or something similar—of men like so-and-so.”
I said:
“O Messenger of Allah, if so-and-so is like that, why do you treat him as you do?”
He replied:
“He is the leader of his people, so through him I seek to win their hearts.”
Authentic: Narrated by Ibn Wahb in al-Jāmiʿ (34).

١٥١٢٤ — عن أسماء بنت يزيد أن النبي ﷺ قال:
((ألا أخبركم بخياركم؟)).
قالوا: بلى يا رسول اللّٰه. قال:
((الذين إذا رؤوا ذكر اللّٰه تعالى)).
ثم قال:
((ألا أخبركم بشراركم؟ المشاؤون بالنميمة، المفسدون بين الأحبة، الباغون للبرآء العنت)).
حسن: رواه أحمد (٢٧٥٩٩) - واللفظ له -، وابن ماجه (٤١١٩)، والبخاري في الأدب المفرد (٣٢٣).

A man asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, who are the allies of Allah?”
He replied:
“Those who, when they are seen, Allah is remembered.”
Good: Narrated by al-Bazzār, as cited in Kashf al-Astār (3626), al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (12325), and Ibn Ṣāʿid in his additions to Ibn al-Mubārak’s al-Zuhd (218).

١٥١٢٦ — عن جرير بن عبد اللّٰه البجلي، عن النبي ﷺ قال:
((من يتزود في الدنيا ينفعه في الآخرة)).
حسن: رواه الطبراني في الكبير (٢/٣٤٥-٣٤٦).
قوله: “من يتزود في الدنيا”: يعني من الأعمال الصالحة.

15126 — Jarīr ibn ʿAbdullāh al-Bajalī narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Whatever provision a person takes in this world will benefit him in the Hereafter.”
Good: Narrated by al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (2/345–346).
The phrase “takes provision in this world” means provision in the form of righteous deeds.

١٥١٢٧ — عن عمر بن الخطاب قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((لو أنكم توكلون على اللّٰه حق توكله، لرزقكم كما يرزق الطير، تغدو خماصًا وتروح بطانًا)).
صحيح: رواه الترمذي (٢٣٤٤)، وابن ماجه (٤١٦٤)، وأحمد (٢٠٥)، وابن حبان (٧٣٠)، والحاكم (٤/٣١٨).
قوله: “خماصًا”: أي ضامرة البطون من الجوع. وقوله: “بطانًا”: أي ممتلئة البطون.

15127 — ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“If you were to rely upon Allah with true reliance, He would provide for you just as He provides for the birds: they leave in the morning with empty stomachs and return in the evening with full stomachs.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (2344), Ibn Mājah (4164), Aḥmad (205), Ibn Ḥibbān (730), and al-Ḥākim (4/318).
The word “khimāṣan” means with stomachs empty and drawn in from hunger.
The word “biṭānan” means with stomachs full.

١٥١٢٨ — عن أنس بن مالك قال: كان أخوان على عهد النبي ﷺ، فكان أحدهما يأتي النبي ﷺ، والآخر يحترف، فشكا المحترف أخاه إلى النبي ﷺ، فقال:
((لعلك ترزق به)).
صحيح: رواه الترمذي (٢٣٤٥)، والبزار (٦٩٨٨)، وصححه الحاكم (١/٩٣).

15128 — Anas ibn Mālik narrated:
There were two brothers during the time of the Prophet ﷺ. One of them would regularly come to the Prophet ﷺ, while the other worked to earn a living.
The one who worked complained to the Prophet ﷺ about his brother.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Perhaps you are being provided for because of him.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (2345), al-Bazzār (6988), and authenticated by al-Ḥākim (1/93).

15129 — ʿAmr ibn Umayyah al-Ḍamrī narrated:
A man asked the Prophet ﷺ:
“Should I leave my camel untied and rely upon Allah?”
He replied:
“Tie it, and rely upon Allah.”
Good: Narrated by Ibn Abī ʿĀṣim in al-Āḥād wa-al-Mathānī (970), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (731) and al-Ḥākim (3/623).

((بسم اللّٰه، توكلت على اللّٰه، اللهم إنا نعوذ بك من أن نزل أو نضل، أو نظلم أو نظلم، أو نجهل أو يجهل علينا)).

معنى التوكل: ليس التوكل القعود عن الكسب، بل التوكل: هو السعي والجهد في طلب الرزق من الطرق المشروعة، ثم التفويض إلى اللّٰه ما قدره له.
روي عن عمر بن الخطاب أنه لقي أناسًا من أهل اليمن، فقال: من أنتم؟ قالوا: نحن المتوكلون. قال: بل أنتم المتكلون، إنما المتوكل الذي يلقي حبه في الأرض، ويتوكل على اللّٰه عز وجل.
رواه ابن أبي الدنيا في التوكل (١٠) بإسناده عن معاوية بن قرة أن عمر بن الخطاب لقي ناسًا فذكره.

وقال عبد اللّٰه بن مسعود: إن أشد آية في القرآن تفويضًا:
﴿وَمَنْ يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللّٰهِ فَهُوَ حَسْبُهُ﴾ [الطلاق: ٣].

15130 — Umm Salamah narrated that when the Prophet ﷺ left his house, he would say:
“In the name of Allah. I place my trust in Allah. O Allah, we seek refuge in You from slipping or going astray, from wronging or being wronged, and from acting ignorantly or having ignorance directed against us.”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (5094), al-Tirmidhī (3427), al-Nasāʾī (5486), Ibn Mājah (3884), Aḥmad (26616, 26704), Ibn al-Sunnī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa-al-Laylah (177), and al-Ḥākim (1/519). The wording is that of al-Tirmidhī.
The Meaning of Reliance upon Allah
Reliance upon Allah does not mean abandoning work and sitting idle.
Rather, reliance means striving and exerting effort in seeking provision through lawful means, then entrusting to Allah whatever He has decreed for the person.
It is narrated that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb met some people from Yemen and asked:
“Who are you?”
They replied:
“We are those who rely upon Allah.”
He said:
“Rather, you are merely dependent upon others. The one who truly relies upon Allah is the one who casts his seed into the earth and then relies upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic.”
Narrated by Ibn Abī al-Dunyā in al-Tawakkul (10), through Muʿāwiyah ibn Qurrah, who narrated that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb met some people and then related the report.
Muʿāwiyah ibn Qurrah did not meet ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, because he was born in the year 37 AH.
ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd said:
“The verse in the Qur’an containing the strongest meaning of entrusting one’s affairs to Allah is: ‘Whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him.’”
 [Sūrat al-Ṭalāq 65:3]
In another narration:
“Whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out.”
 [Sūrat al-Ṭalāq 65:2]
This was mentioned by Ibn Abī al-Dunyā in al-Tawakkul (50), ʿAbd al-Razzāq (3/370–371), and others.
Some sages said that reliance upon Allah has three levels:
The first is abandoning complaint.
The second is contentment.
The third is love.
Abandoning complaint is the level of patience.
Contentment is the heart becoming tranquil with whatever Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has apportioned for it, and this is higher than the first level.
Love is that a person loves whatever Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does with him.
The first level is for the ascetics, the second for the truthful, and the third for the messengers.
Ibn Abī al-Dunyā mentioned this in al-Tawakkul (46).

 [Sūrat al-Ṭalāq 65:2]
This was mentioned by Ibn Abī al-Dunyā in al-Tawakkul (50), ʿAbd al-Razzāq (3/370–371), and others.
Some sages said that reliance upon Allah has three levels:
The first is abandoning complaint.
The second is contentment.
The third is love.
Abandoning complaint is the level of patience.
Contentment is the heart becoming tranquil with whatever Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has apportioned for it, and this is higher than the first level.
Love is that a person loves whatever Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does with him.
The first level is for the ascetics, the second for the truthful, and the third for the messengers.
Ibn Abī al-Dunyā mentioned this in al-Tawakkul (46).

١٥١٣٢ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن بسر قال: أتى النبي ﷺ أعرابيان، فقال أحدهما: من خير الرجال يا محمد؟ قال النبي ﷺ:
((من طال عمره وحسن عمله)).
وقال الآخر: إن شرائع الإسلام قد كثرت علينا، فباب نتمسك به جامع؟ قال:
((لا يزال لسانك رطبًا من ذكر اللّٰه)).
صحيح: رواه الترمذي (٢٣٢٩، ٣٣٧٥)، وأحمد (١٧٦٨٠، ١٧٦٩٨) - والسياق له -.

15132 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Busr narrated:
Two Bedouins came to the Prophet ﷺ.
One of them asked:
“Who are the best of men, O Muḥammad?”
The Prophet ﷺ replied:
“The one whose life is long and whose deeds are good.”
The other said:
“The teachings of Islam have become numerous for us. Give us one comprehensive practice to which we can hold fast.”
He replied:
“Let your tongue remain moist with the remembrance of Allah.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (2329, 3375) and Aḥmad (17680, 17698), and this is his wording.

“Shall I tell you who the best among you are?”

15136 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“The lifespans of my Ummah are generally between sixty and seventy years, and few of them will exceed that.”
Good: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (3550), Ibn Mājah (4236), Ibn Ḥibbān (2980), and al-Ḥākim (2/427).

١٥١٣٧ — عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي ﷺ قال:
((أعذر اللّٰه إلى امرئ أخر أجله حتى بلغه ستين سنة)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٦٤١٩).
وفي رواية عند أحمد (٧٧١٣) من وجه آخر عن سعيد المقبري، عن أبي هريرة:
((لقد أعذر اللّٰه إلى عبد أحياه حتى بلغه ستين أو سبعين سنة، لقد أعذر اللّٰه إليه، لقد أعذر اللّٰه إليه)).
ومعنى الحديث: أن العبد إذا بلغ ستين سنة ولم يتب عن المعصية فليس له عند اللّٰه عذر على معصيته.

15137 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Allah has left no excuse for a person whose life He prolongs until he reaches sixty years of age.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6419).
In another narration recorded by Aḥmad (7713), through a different route from Saʿīd al-Maqburī, from Abū Hurayrah:
“Allah has truly left no excuse for a servant whom He allows to live until sixty or seventy years of age. Allah has indeed left him no excuse; Allah has indeed left him no excuse.”
The meaning of the hadith is that if a servant reaches sixty years of age and still does not repent from sin, he has no excuse before Allah for persisting in disobedience.

١٥١٣٨ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((انظروا إلى من أسفل منكم، ولا تنظروا إلى من هو فوقكم، فهو أجدر أن لا تزدروا نعمة اللّٰه عليكم)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٩٦٣: ٩).
قوله: “انظروا إلى من أسفل منكم”: أي في أمور الدنيا، وأما أمور الدين فلينظر إلى من هو فوقه.
وقوله: “تزدروا”: أي لا تحتقروا.

15138 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Look at those who are below you, and do not look at those who are above you, for that is more likely to keep you from belittling Allah’s blessing upon you.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2963:9).
The words “look at those who are below you” refer to worldly matters. As for matters of religion, a person should look to those who are above him.
The word “tazdarū” means to regard as insignificant or belittle.

١٥١٣٩ — عن أبي هريرة أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قال:
((إذا نظر أحدكم إلى من فضل عليه في المال والخلق فلينظر إلى من هو أسفل منه ممن فضل عليه)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٤٩٠)، ومسلم (٢٩٦٣: ٨).

15139 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“If one of you looks at someone who has been given more than him in wealth or physical appearance, let him look at someone below him over whom he himself has been favored.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6490) and Muslim (2963:8).

15140 — Abū Dharr narrated:
The Prophet ﷺ, my beloved friend, instructed me with seven things. Among them was:
“He instructed me to look at those who are below me and not to look at those who are above me.”
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (21415), al-Nasāʾī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa-al-Laylah (354), authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (449), and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Duʿāʾ (1648).

١٥١٤١ — عن ابن أبان قال: أتيت عثمان بن عفان بطهور، وهو جالس على المقاعد، فتوضأ، فأحسن الوضوء، ثم قال: رأيت النبي ﷺ توضأ، وهو في هذا المجلس، فأحسن الوضوء، ثم قال:
((من توضأ مثل هذا الوضوء ثم أتى المسجد، فركع ركعتين، ثم جلس، غفر له ما تقدم من ذنبه)).
قال: وقال النبي ﷺ:
((لا تغتروا)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٦٤٣٣).

15141 — Ibn Abān narrated:
I brought water for ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān while he was sitting at al-Maqāʿid.
He performed wuḍūʾ and perfected it.
Then he said:
“I saw the Prophet ﷺ perform wuḍūʾ while sitting in this very place, and he perfected his wuḍūʾ.”
Then the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Whoever performs wuḍūʾ like this, then comes to the mosque, prays two rakʿahs, and then sits, his previous sins will be forgiven.”
Then the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Do not become deceived by this.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6433).

١٥١٤٢ — عن أبي هريرة قال: سمعت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يقول:
((لن يدخل أحدًا عمله الجنة)).
قالوا: ولا أنت يا رسول اللّٰه؟ قال:
((لا، ولا أنا، إلا أن يتغمدني اللّٰه بفضل ورحمة، فسددوا وقاربوا، ولا يتمنين أحدكم الموت، إما محسنًا فلعله أن يزداد خيرًا، وإما مسيئًا فلعله أن يستعتب)).

“None of your deeds will save you.”
They asked:
“Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?”
He replied:
“Not even me, unless Allah envelops me in mercy. So remain upright and come as close as you can. Worship in the morning, in the evening, and during part of the night. Keep to moderation, keep to moderation, and you will reach your goal.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6463).

١٥١٤٤ — عن عائشة قالت: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((سددوا وقاربوا وأبشروا، فإنه لن يدخل الجنة أحدًا عمله)).
قالوا: ولا أنت يا رسول اللّٰه؟ قال:
((ولا أنا، إلا أن يتغمدني اللّٰه منه برحمة، واعلموا أن أحب العمل إلى اللّٰه أدومه وإن قل)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٤٦٤، ٦٤٦٧)، ومسلم (٢٨١٨)، والسياق لمسلم.

15144 — ʿĀʾishah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Remain upright, come as close as you can, and rejoice, for no one’s deeds will cause him to enter Paradise.”
They asked:
“Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?”
He replied:
“Not even me, unless Allah envelops me in mercy from Him. And know that the deeds most beloved to Allah are those performed most consistently, even if they are few.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6464, 6467) and Muslim (2818). The context is that of Muslim.

١٥١٤٥ — عن أنس قال: إنكم لتعملون أعمالًا هي أدق في أعينكم من الشعر، إن كنا لنعدها على عهد النبي ﷺ من الموبقات.
قال أبو عبد اللّٰه - وهو البخاري -: يعني بذلك المهلكات.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٦٤٩٢).

english_source:
15145 — Anas said:
“You commit deeds that appear in your eyes to be finer than a hair, yet during the time of the Prophet ﷺ we used to count them among the destructive sins.”
Abū ʿAbdullāh—meaning al-Bukhārī—said:
“By this he means sins that lead to destruction.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6492).

١٥١٤٦ — عن سهل بن سعد قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((إياكم ومحقرات الذنوب، كقوم نزلوا في بطن واد، فجاء ذا بعود، وجاء ذا بعود، حتى أنضجوا خبزتهم، وإن محقرات الذنوب متى يؤخذ بها صاحبها تهلكه)).
صحيح: رواه أحمد (٢٢٨٠٨)، والرامهرمزي في الأمثال (٦٧)، والبيهقي في الشعب (٧٢٦٧).

english_source:
15146 — Sahl ibn Saʿd narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Beware of sins that are regarded as insignificant. They are like a group of people who camp in the bottom of a valley: one man brings a stick, another brings a stick, until together they gather enough to cook their bread. Likewise, when a person is taken to account for seemingly insignificant sins, they can destroy him.”
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (22808), al-Rāmahurmuzī in al-Amthāl (67), and al-Bayhaqī in Shuʿab al-Īmān (7267).

“There are two blessings in which many people suffer loss: health and free time.”

١٥١٤٨ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن عمرو بن العاص قال: قال لي رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((أما علمت أن الإسلام يهدم ما كان قبله، وأن الهجرة تهدم ما كان قبلها، وأن الحج يهدم ما كان قبله)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٢١: ١٩٢).

١٥١٤٩ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن مسعود قال: قال أناس لرسول اللّٰه ﷺ: يا رسول اللّٰه، أنؤاخذ بما عملنا في الجاهلية؟ قال:
((أما من أحسن منكم في الإسلام فلا يؤاخذ بها، ومن أساء أخذ بعمله في الجاهلية والإسلام)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٩٢١)، ومسلم (١٢٠: ١٨٩).
التوفيق بين الحديثين: الحديث الأول يدل على الثبات على الإسلام، والحديث الثاني فيه إشارة إلى الارتداد أو الشرك، فإن من ارتد أو أشرك أخذ بما عمل في الجاهلية والإسلام من أعمال سوء. وقد ذكره البخاري في استتابة المرتدين.

15149 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd narrated:
Some people asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:
“O Messenger of Allah, will we be held accountable for what we did during jāhiliyyah?”
He replied:
“Whoever among you does well after entering Islam will not be taken to account for those deeds. But whoever does evil will be taken to account for what he did both in jāhiliyyah and in Islam.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6921) and Muslim (120:189).
The reconciliation between the two hadiths is that the first refers to one who remains firm upon Islam.
The second contains an indication concerning apostasy or shirk: if a person apostatizes or commits shirk, he may be taken to account for the evil deeds he committed both during jāhiliyyah and after entering Islam.
Al-Bukhārī included this narration in his chapter concerning seeking repentance from apostates.

١٥١٥٠ — عن أبي هريرة أنه سمع النبي ﷺ يقول:
((إن ثلاثة في بني إسرائيل: أبرص وأقرع وأعمى، فأراد اللّٰه أن يبتليهم، فبعث إليهم ملكًا، فأتى الأبرص فقال: أي شيء أحب إليك؟ قال: لون حسن، وجلد حسن، ويذهب عني الذي قد قذرني الناس. قال: فمسحه، فذهب عنه قذره، وأعطي لونًا حسنًا وجلدًا حسنًا. قال: فأي المال أحب إليك؟ قال: الإبل - أو قال: البقر - شك إسحاق، إلا أن الأبرص أو الأقرع قال أحدهما: الإبل، وقال الآخر: البقر. قال: فأعطي ناقة عشراء، فقال: بارك اللّٰه لك فيها.
قال: فأتى الأقرع فقال: أي شيء أحب إليك؟ قال: شعر حسن، ويذهب عني هذا الذي قذرني الناس. قال: فمسحه، فذهب عنه، وأعطي شعرًا حسنًا. قال: فأي المال أحب إليك؟ قال: البقر. فأعطي بقرة حاملًا، فقال: بارك اللّٰه لك فيها.
قال: فأتى الأعمى فقال: أي شيء أحب إليك؟ قال: أن يرد اللّٰه إلي بصري فأبصر به الناس. قال: فمسحه، فرد اللّٰه إليه بصره. قال: فأي المال أحب إليك؟ قال: الغنم. فأعطي شاة والدًا. فأنتج هذان، وولد هذا، قال: فكان لهذا واد من الإبل، ولهذا واد من البقر، ولهذا واد من الغنم.
قال: ثم إنه أتى الأبرص في صورته وهيئته، فقال: رجل مسكين، قد انقطعت بي الحبال في سفري، فلا بلاغ لي اليوم إلا باللّٰه ثم بك، أسألك بالذي أعطاك اللون الحسن والجلد الحسن والمال، بعيرًا أتبلغ عليه في سفري. فقال: الحقوق كثيرة. فقال له: كأني أعرفك، ألم تكن أبرص يقذرك الناس، فقيرًا فأعطاك اللّٰه؟ فقال: إنما ورثت هذا المال كابرًا عن كابر. فقال: إن كنت كاذبًا فصيرك اللّٰه إلى ما كنت.
قال: وأتى الأقرع في صورته، فقال له مثل ما قال لهذا، ورد عليه مثل ما رد على هذا، فقال: إن كنت كاذبًا فصيرك اللّٰه إلى ما كنت.
قال: وأتى الأعمى في صورته وهيئته، فقال: رجل مسكين وابن سبيل، انقطعت بي الحبال في سفري، فلا بلاغ لي اليوم إلا باللّٰه ثم بك، أسألك بالذي رد عليك بصرك شاة أتبلغ بها في سفري. فقال: قد كنت أعمى فرد اللّٰه إلي بصري، فخذ ما شئت، ودع ما شئت، فواللّٰه لا أجهدك اليوم بشيء أخذته للّٰه. فقال: أمسك مالك، فإنما ابتليتم، فقد رضي عنك وسخط على صاحبيك)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٤٦٤)، ومسلم (٢٩٦٤).

15150 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say:
“There were three men among the Children of Israel: a leper, a bald man, and a blind man. Allah wished to test them, so He sent an angel to them.
The angel came to the leper and asked: ‘What would you love most?’
He replied: ‘A beautiful complexion, healthy skin, and that this condition because of which people find me repulsive be removed from me.’
The angel touched him, his affliction disappeared, and he was given beautiful skin and a fine complexion.
The angel asked: ‘What kind of wealth do you love most?’
He replied: ‘Camels’—or he said: ‘Cattle.’”
Isḥāq, one of the narrators, was uncertain, except that one of the leper and the bald man said camels and the other said cattle.
“He was given a pregnant she-camel and the angel said: ‘May Allah bless it for you.’
Then he came to the bald man and asked: ‘What would you love most?’
He replied: ‘Beautiful hair and that this condition because of which people find me repulsive be removed from me.’
The angel touched him, his affliction disappeared, and he was given beautiful hair.
He asked: ‘What kind of wealth do you love most?’
He replied: ‘Cattle.’
So he was given a pregnant cow, and the angel said: ‘May Allah bless it for you.’
Then he came to the blind man and asked: ‘What would you love most?’
He replied: ‘That Allah restore my sight so that I may see people.’
The angel touched him, and Allah restored his sight.
He asked: ‘What kind of wealth do you love most?’
He replied: ‘Sheep.’
So he was given a sheep that was giving birth.”
The animals multiplied until the first had a valley full of camels, the second a valley full of cattle, and the third a valley full of sheep.
“Then the angel came to the former leper in the same appearance and condition that the man had once had. He said: ‘I am a poor traveler whose means have been cut off during my journey. Today I have no means of reaching my destination except through Allah and then through you. I ask you by the One who gave you beautiful skin, a fine complexion, and wealth to give me a camel upon which I may continue my journey.’
The man replied: ‘There are many obligations upon my wealth.’
The angel said: ‘I think I recognize you. Were you not once a leper whom people found repulsive, poor, and then Allah gave you wealth?’
He replied: ‘I merely inherited this wealth from my forefathers.’
The angel said: ‘If you are lying, may Allah return you to what you were.’
Then he came to the former bald man in his previous appearance and said the same thing to him. The man responded in the same way, so the angel said: ‘If you are lying, may Allah return you to what you were.’
Then he came to the former blind man in the same appearance and condition that he had once had. He said: ‘I am a poor traveler whose means have been cut off during my journey. Today I have no means of reaching my destination except through Allah and then through you. I ask you by the One who restored your sight to give me one sheep by which I may continue my journey.’
The man replied: ‘I was indeed blind, and Allah restored my sight. Take whatever you wish and leave whatever you wish. By Allah, today I will not make things difficult for you concerning anything you take for the sake of Allah.’
The angel said: ‘Keep your wealth. You were only being tested. Allah is pleased with you and angry with your two companions.’”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3464) and Muslim (2964).
